opportunities.title: Undergraduate Tuition Fee Grants

amount.raw: Our grants cover the cost of tuition fees, up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Individuals from low-income households who are ordinarily resident in Scotland (with a Scottish connection), not eligible for government funding for tuition fees, and enrolled on (or holding an unconditional offer for) an eligible undergraduate degree course at a Scottish Higher Education Institution.
opportunities.summary: Grants covering tuition fees for undergraduate degree study at eligible Scottish Higher Education Institutions for students from low-income households who are ineligible for government tuition fee support. The application portal is open from 1 June 2026 to 5pm 1 December 2026 for academic year 2026-27.
discipline_tags: Second-degree reskilling in skills-shortage areas (medicine, health, social work, IT/computing, engineering, quantitative sciences, geosciences, biosciences, cultural/creative studies)

opportunities.funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
opportunities.title: Carnegie-Morgan Scholarship

amount.raw: Full tuition fees for the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants and an additional living-cost bursary of £1,200.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scottish-domiciled students from low-income households who have been accepted onto the MSc Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants (full-time or part-time), are ordinarily resident in Scotland, entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK, and have not already obtained a postgraduate degree.
opportunities.summary: Scholarship in partnership with the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh for the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants (awarded by the University of Edinburgh), covering full tuition fees plus a £1,200 living-cost bursary, to widen participation in postgraduate plant science and support Scotland's net-zero and biodiversity goals. Rolling opportunity tied to admission to the MSc course.
